review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp attributes on the related lemmas in ContinuousMap/Basic.lean, Bounded/Basic.lean, Bounded/Normed.lean and Data/SetLike/Basic.lean. The @[simp] lemmas here (norm_smul_const, the linearIsometryBoundedOfCompact_* rfl lemmas, norm_mkOfCompact and the others) look reasonably oriented. I found no cycle risk and no unwanted expansion. The two findings are a documented non-confluence that is worked around locally, and a missing simp attribute on one lemma whose siblings are all simp. I couldn't run Lean, so I did not test whether the proposed simp attribute causes any simp-set conflict, and I have not confirmed the exact mechanism of the non-confluence.

findings.problem: A comment records a simp non-confluence. The default simp lemma `SetLike.coe_sort_coe` rewrites the type `↥(K : Set X)` to `↥K`, and this blocks the simp lemma `ContinuousMap.restrict_apply`. That lemma is stated for `s : Set α` and `x : s`. For `K : Compacts X`, the restricted functions `restrict K (F i)` therefore can't use the canonical simp lemma unless the user removes a global simp lemma by hand. The simp interface has no `restrict_apply` form that fits `SetLike` subsets. The same problem will hit any other use of `f.restrict K` with `K : Compacts X`, such as `norm_restrict_mono_set` in this file.
findings.proposed_change: Add a simp-normal lemma for the coerced-`SetLike` form, for example `restrict_apply` stated with `(s : S) [SetLike S α]` and `x : s`, or an `@[simp]` variant `restrict_apply_setLike`, in ContinuousMap/Basic.lean. Then both `simp` and `simp [-SetLike.coe_sort_coe]` give `f.restrict K x = f x`. Or make the simp set confluent in another way, so the `-SetLike.coe_sort_coe` workaround and the TODO can be dropped.
findings.benefit: Plain `simp` would work on `restrict` applied to `Compacts` and other SetLike subsets. Users would no longer need to know to remove a global simp lemma. The TODO about non-confluence would be resolved.

findings.problem: `mkOfCompact_star` is the `star` analogue of `mkOfCompact_add`, `mkOfCompact_neg`, `mkOfCompact_sub` and `mkOfCompact_one`. All of those are `@[simp]` rfl-lemmas pushing `mkOfCompact` through an operation. `mkOfCompact_star` has no simp attribute, so a simp-normal-form expression like `mkOfCompact (star f)` doesn't reduce to `star (mkOfCompact f)`. The file's own proof of `NormedStarGroup` has to name it in an explicit `rw`.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[simp]`, as for the other `mkOfCompact_*` homomorphism lemmas, and consider moving it to Bounded/Star.lean next to the other `mkOfCompact` lemmas. The simp set would then treat `mkOfCompact` uniformly across add, neg, sub, one and star.
findings.benefit: `simp` would push `mkOfCompact` through `star` consistently with the other operations. It would also remove an unannounced inconsistency in the simp interface, and the explicit `rw [BoundedContinuousFunction.mkOfCompact_star, ...]` could become simp.
